title: Ulyana and the Letters
premise: Wren Halloran, a widowed single father running the last bookshop in Alder Bay, agrees to a fake date with Ulyana Marsh to survive the Halloran family reunion, where his mother is pressuring him to sell the shop and move closer to 'family.' Ulyana, newly returned to town to settle her late grandmother's estate, is hiding letters her grandmother left behind—letters that reveal Wren's late wife once loved someone else before choosing him. As their pretend romance deepens into something real, Wren must confront his guilt over not being enough for either woman, forgive himself in the mirror, and choose love over duty. The story ends with Wren keeping the bookshop, Ulyana staying in town, and the two of them reading her grandmother's final letter together on the shop's doorstep.
about_author: Hazel Voss is a former small-town librarian who writes romances about second chances and the places that hold our memories. She lives on the coast with her family and an ever-growing stack of unread paperbacks.

chapters.title: The Reunion Clause
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren learns his mother expects him—and his daughter Poppy—at the Halloran reunion, where she plans to announce the sale of the family property he's been quietly renting for his bookshop. Panicked at facing relatives alone, he blurts out that he's seeing someone. Emotional beat: dread masked as control.

chapters.title: A Stranger with Good Posture
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Ulyana arrives in Alder Bay to sort through her grandmother's house and wanders into Wren's bookshop seeking shelter from rain. When he awkwardly proposes a fake date, she surprises herself by saying yes—she needs a reason to avoid her own meddling aunt. Emotional beat: wary curiosity sparking into mischief.

chapters.title: Dessert Was Never Part of the Deal
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At the reunion, their performance is flawless until dessert, when Wren's mother corners them and Ulyana defends the bookshop with unexpected ferocity. Walking home, neither can remember where the act ended. Emotional beat: the fake date curdling sweetly into real want.

chapters.title: Letters in the Linen Closet
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Sorting her grandmother's belongings, Ulyana finds a bundle of unsent letters addressed to a man named Halloran—written decades ago, and one written only two years back. She hides them, unsettled. Emotional beat: the past pressing its palm against the present.

chapters.title: Poppy's Library Card
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Poppy, eight and sharp-eyed, asks why Miss Marsh keeps coming back if it's all pretend. Wren deflects, but that night he rereads his late wife's old journal and finds an unfamiliar name in it. Emotional beat: grief loosening its grip just enough to hurt differently.

chapters.title: The Second Date They Don't Call a Date
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. A 'planning session' for another fake event becomes a real evening: takeout among the bookshelves while Poppy sleeps. Ulyana almost shows him the letters; Wren almost tells her about the journal. Both retreat. Emotional beat: intimacy outrunning honesty.

chapters.title: What Margaret Knew
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Ulyana finally reads the letters fully: her grandmother loved Wren's father first, gave him up for duty, and watched the Hallorans from afar her whole life—including Wren's marriage. The last letter warns against repeating her mistake. Emotional beat: inheritance as warning, not wound.

chapters.title: Sold, Pending Signatures
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. His mother arrives with the buyer's paperwork and reveals she knows the 'girlfriend' was staged—she saw the reunion photos and read the truth in his face anyway. She gives him thirty days to prove the shop can survive. Emotional beat: humiliation cracking open into resolve.

chapters.title: The Mirror Argument
chapters.summary: Climax. After a public argument where Ulyana accuses him of hiding behind grief and duty, Wren faces himself—literally—in the shop window and admits he chose invisibility long before his wife died. He writes his own letter, to her, saying goodbye. Emotional beat: forgiveness beginning at home.

chapters.title: Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Resolution. Wren hosts a community night that saves the shop; his mother signs instead a lease making it permanent. On the doorstep, Ulyana reads her grandmother's final letter aloud, and Wren answers it with a kiss and a promise to stop training his heart to stay quiet. Emotional beat: love chosen, openly, at last.
